info.title: WorkAdventure Admin API
info.description:
This is a documentation about the endpoints of the admin API called by WorkAdventure. Most are called by the pusher, a few by the back. 
 You can find out more about WorkAdventure on [github](https://github.com/thecodingmachine/workadventure).

streamId.description: The WebRTC stream this sample measures.

connectionId.description: Peer connection the stream rode on.

remoteUserUuid.description: The other party. Pseudonymized admin-side for worlds that opted out of user-level activity.

remoteSpaceUserId.description: The other party's space-scoped id. Null on an outbound sample: a stream published to a LiveKit server has no single remote user.

spaceName.description: Space the stream belongs to. The pusher rejects a sample for a space the socket has not joined.

streamCategory.description: Whether the stream is a camera or a screen share.

transportType.description: Direct peer connection, or relayed through an SFU.

direction.description: Whether the sample measures a stream we receive or one we send. An outbound sample describes our own encoder, so it carries no jitter and no remote user.

relay.description: Whether the connection went through a TURN relay.

livekitServerUrl.description: LiveKit server that carried the stream, when applicable.

livekitRegion.description: Region of the LiveKit server the client was connected to: set by LiveKit Cloud, null on P2P streams and usually on a self-hosted server.

fps.description: Frames per second observed over the sample window.

fpsStdDev.description: Jitter in the frame rate; a high value reads as stutter even when the mean fps looks fine.

bandwidthBytesPerSecond.description: Throughput observed over the sample window.

qualityLimitationReason.description: Outbound only: why the browser is degrading what it encodes. `cpu` is a machine that cannot keep up, which otherwise reads to everyone else as a bad network.

encoderImplementation.description: Outbound only: encoder the browser picked, e.g. "libaom", "libvpx", "ExternalEncoder".

windowSeconds.description: Inbound only: time covered by the playback counters below, i.e. since this stream's previous sample. Null when the window is not measurable (first sample, counters restarted, right after a deliberate pause), which nulls every counter below. Divide summed counters by summed windows, never average per-sample ratios.

framesDecoded.description: Inbound only: frames decoded during the window. 0 while video was expected means the stream stalled; a stall that never resumes shows only here, since the browser counts freezes and pauses when the next frame arrives.

framesDropped.description: Inbound only: frames the receiver dropped during the window (before decoding, or too late to display).

freezeCount.description: Inbound only: freezes during the window, as the browser defines them: a gap between two rendered frames of max(3 × the average frame duration, average + 150 ms), up to 5 s. Counted when the next frame is rendered. Null when the browser does not report it.

freezeSeconds.description: Inbound only: total duration of those freezes, in seconds.

pauseCount.description: Inbound only: gaps longer than 5 s between two rendered frames (never counted as freezes). Pauses we caused are excluded: no sample is sent while we pause a stream on purpose, nor right after.

pauseSeconds.description: Inbound only: total duration of those pauses. Counted when the video resumes, so it can exceed windowSeconds.

interFrameDelaySumSeconds.description: Inbound only: sum of the delays between consecutive rendered frames during the window. With the squared sum and framesDecoded, gives the per-frame delay variance: Σd²/n − (Σd/n)².

interFrameDelaySquaredSumSeconds.description: Inbound only: sum of the squared delays between consecutive rendered frames during the window.

decodeSeconds.description: Inbound only: time spent decoding during the window. Divided by framesDecoded: the receiver's decode cost per frame, which depends on codec and resolution.

captureFps.description: Outbound only, over the last second like fps: frames per second the camera or screen capture delivered to the encoder (RTCVideoSourceStats). Against captureTargetFps, tells a camera that starves the encoder (dim light, overloaded machine) from an encoder dropping frames. A screen capture only delivers frames when the content changes.

captureTargetFps.description: Outbound only: frame rate the capture is configured at (MediaTrackSettings.frameRate).

encodeMsPerFrame.description: Outbound only, over the last second: encoding time per encoded frame, all simulcast/SVC layers together, in milliseconds.

cpuLimitedRatio.description: Outbound only, over the last second: share of the time (0 to 1) the browser degraded the stream for lack of CPU (qualityLimitationDurations), where qualityLimitationReason is only a snapshot.

bandwidthLimitedRatio.description: Outbound only, over the last second: share of the time (0 to 1) the browser degraded the stream for lack of bandwidth.

packetsReceived.description: Inbound only, over windowSeconds like the playback counters: RTP packets of the video received.

packetsLost.description: Inbound only, over windowSeconds: RTP packets of the video lost on the way to us. Loss share = Σ packetsLost / Σ (packetsLost + packetsReceived). A packet counted as lost then received late is taken back, never below 0.

roundTripTimeMs.description: Inbound only: round-trip time of the connection the stream arrives on (selected ICE candidate pair) when the sample was taken: to the peer or its TURN relay in P2P, to the SFU otherwise.

uploadRoundTripTimeMs.description: Outbound only: round-trip time to the other end (peer or SFU), from its latest receiver report about the largest layer.

uploadLossRatio.description: Outbound only: share of the packets (0 to 1) the other end reported lost in its latest receiver report about the largest layer.

availableOutgoingBitrate.description: Outbound only: the browser's estimate of the bandwidth it can send on this connection, in bits per second.

sampleSeq.description: Monotonic counter per stream, used to order and de-duplicate samples.

meetingKind.description: What the meeting was: a spontaneous proximity bubble, an area people went to in order to meet, the world megaphone, a speaker zone, or `external`. Megaphone and speaker zone are broadcasts — a meeting whose predicate is one speaker on air rather than two people present — so anything reading meeting time as conversation time filters them out. `external` is an area that opens a meeting somewhere else entirely (Teams, Google Meet), where what is measured is time spent in the AREA and not in the call, which happens in another tab or another app. Filled by the back from what the space's client declared; by the client for the ones the back cannot see (Jitsi, Teams, Google Meet).

webrtcSeconds.description: Seconds carried peer-to-peer over WebRTC. With livekitSeconds, adds up to durationSeconds unless the space had no media at all. Filled by the back only.

endReason.description: `socket_closed` and the `pusher_*` values mean the client never got to close it — a tab closed mid-meeting, or the pusher restarted.

oneOf.description: A meeting, measured. One row per meeting — by the back, which owns the meeting's lifecycle and counts its participants; the row is attributed to nobody, because a meeting belongs to no one participant. Rows without `meetingKind` were opened by a client, once per participant, and carry participant-seconds: Jitsi meetings, and every row older than the back-emitted ones. A broadcast is the same row under a `megaphone` or `speaker_zone` kind: from the first speaker going on air to the last going off, and an empty megaphone space accrues nothing.

meetingKind.description: What the meeting was: a bubble, an area, the world megaphone, a speaker zone, or `external`. Megaphone and speaker zone are broadcasts, `external` a meeting held elsewhere; see meeting.ended.

role.description: `speaker` if they were on air at any point; a panelist who also listened to the others is a speaker. In a bubble or an area everyone is on air, so it is always `speaker` there — it only distinguishes anyone under a broadcast kind.

webrtcSeconds.description: Seconds carried peer-to-peer over WebRTC. With livekitSeconds, adds up to durationSeconds unless the space had no media at all. Filled by the back only.

livekitSeconds.description: Seconds carried by the LiveKit SFU, which the space switches to past the WebRTC size limit or to record. Filled by the back only.

durationSeconds.description: Length of the interval in seconds — endedAt minus startedAt, reported so nothing has to pair rows.

endReason.description: `back_shutdown` means the server closed it, not the people in it.

oneOf.description: One person's time in one meeting, clipped to it: someone alone in an area before the second person arrived starts when the meeting opens, and a listener present before anyone went on air starts when the broadcast does. Emitted by the back when the meeting ends. Under a broadcast kind this is audience time, reported once per listener: it adds up to reach × duration, not duration. This is the per-user view of a meeting: meeting.ended is deliberately attributed to nobody, because a meeting belongs to no one participant. NOT to be joined to itself: grouping these rows by meetingId yields who was in a meeting with whom, and aggregated over months that is a map of who works with whom — a different product from a record of what happened, and one with a different legal footing. Nothing builds that query today, and the decision to leave it unbuilt is the reason this sentence exists: it is two lines of SQL away, so it will not stay unbuilt by accident.

post.description: Accepts a batch of analytics events collected by one pusher instance. Every event conforms to the shared catalog (AnalyticsEvent): `eventName` is a closed set the pusher validates against before sending, and `source` is pinned per event — `pusher` marks events the pusher synthesized itself, which a socket may never claim and which the admin projects into connection sessions. `properties` is passthrough, so a newer front may add fields to a known event without a lockstep deploy. Best-effort: the pusher retries transient failures and splits a rejected batch to isolate the offending events, so ingestion should be idempotent on `eventId`.

422.description: Invalid payload. The pusher responds by re-sending the batch one event at a time to isolate the offending events — see sendEventsIndividually.

post.description:
Notifies the admin that a recording egress ended, so it can be turned into a
customer-facing webhook. Only the end of an egress is reported, whether it succeeded
or not: read `status` to tell a usable recording from a failed one.
Retried 3 times on transport or 5xx errors; a 4xx is taken as a definitive rejection
and is not retried. Never called when ADMIN_API_URL is unset.

phase.description: Always `ended`. Nothing is sent when an egress starts.

status.description: The LiveKit egress status. `EGRESS_COMPLETE` means the recording is usable.

recordingSessionId.description: The WorkAdventure recording session this egress belongs to.

playUri.description: The full URL of the room that was recorded.

recorder.description: The user who started the recording.

startedAt.description: When the egress started, ISO 8601. Null when LiveKit did not report it.

endedAt.description: When the egress ended, ISO 8601. Null when LiveKit did not report it.

error.description: The LiveKit error message when the egress failed, null otherwise.

files.description: The files LiveKit wrote. Empty when the egress failed.

filename.description: The object key LiveKit wrote in the configured storage.

durationSeconds.description: The recording duration, rounded to the second.

200.description: The event has been taken into account.

4XX.description:
The event is rejected. The back does not retry, and the notification is lost:
only answer a 4xx for a payload you will never accept.

5XX.description: Transient failure. The back retries 3 times (250 ms, 1 s, 4 s) before giving up.
